title: Insulation Rebates in Richmond 2026: Up to $5,500 from BC Hydro
desc: Richmond is flat, low and close to the water, with 7,175 owner-occupied houses built before 1981. BC Hydro's insulation rebate formula and what to ask about crawlspaces.
lead: Richmond sits on a flat river delta. If your house has a crawlspace, floor and crawlspace insulation belongs on the list alongside the attic.
cards_heading: What BC Hydro pays for insulation in Richmond
cards_intro: Amounts come from BC Hydro's insulation page, re-read on October 2, 2026. They apply to owner-held homes heated mainly by electricity. Gas-heated homes can look at FortisBC.

cards.title: Attic
cards.amount: $0.02 x R added x sq ft
cards.note: Capped at $900. New material must add at least R12.

cards.title: Crawlspace and basement walls
cards.amount: $0.09 x R added x sq ft
cards.note: Capped at $1,200. Needs at least R10 added.

cards.title: Exposed floor
cards.amount: $0.07 x R added x sq ft
cards.note: Floors over a crawlspace are in the $1,000 cap line. At least R20 added.

cards.title: Second-upgrade bonus
cards.note: For completing more than one eligible upgrade.

cards.title: Income-qualified
cards.note: A free evaluation and upgrades through BC Hydro and FortisBC.

after_cards:
A crawlspace-first example

Adding R-20 under 1,000 square feet of floor over a crawlspace gives 0.07 x 20 x 1,000 = $1,400, so the $1,000 cap applies. Topping an attic by R-26 over 900 square feet pays 0.02 x 26 x 900 = $468. That is $1,468, from our arithmetic on the published rules.
sections: The 2021 Census counted 81,080 households in Richmond. About 21,040 (26%) live in homes built before 1981, and 7,175 are owner-occupied houses from that era. Another 42% of Richmond households live in apartments and 29% rent, so the pool for this rebate is smaller than the city's size suggests. It is also a place where many residents own, with 71% of households owner-occupied.
Floors can matter as much as attics

Richmond lies on the Fraser River delta. The ground is flat and damp. If your house has a crawlspace, heat and moisture can move through the floor, so the program lines for exposed floors and crawlspace walls deserve a close look. Ask a contractor to inspect the crawlspace before quoting and to explain how they will keep it ventilated and dry.

Moisture problems must be fixed before new insulation goes in. The program does not pay if mould or pests remain.

Richmond's average January low from 2015 to 2024 was 1.5°C and the coldest day was -14.4°C. That is one of the milder records in our BC list. The savings from insulation are real but smaller than in the Interior, so look at the rebate against the quote rather than assuming a quick payback. BC Hydro says upgrades can cut at least 10% of a home's energy cost.

• An electrically heated, owner-held home with a BC Hydro account.
  • A Home Performance Contractor Network installer.
  • An invoice that lists the insulation type, R-value and area.
  • An application within six months of the invoice.
installers_intro: These are Richmond's top-rated insulation companies by Google reviews, weighted by number of reviews. Nobody pays to be here.
claim_steps: Have the contractor inspect the attic and the crawlspace and note the current R-value.
Ask for a priced plan that lists each area with the R-value added.
Make sure the invoice is dated and lists the area for each space.
Add a heat pump or water heater upgrade in the same application if you can.
faq: Does a crawlspace count as eligible?
Yes. Basement and crawlspace walls pay $0.09 per R per square foot up to $1,200, and floors over a crawlspace fall in the $1,000 cap line.
What if the crawlspace is damp?
Fix the moisture first. The program requires that pests and moisture problems be resolved before new insulation goes in.
Can I use this if I own a townhouse in Richmond?
Side-by-side row homes and townhouses can qualify when each unit has its own meter and the account is not in a strata corporation's name. Condos use BC Hydro's separate program.
The average January low from 2015 to 2024 was 1.5°C and the coldest day was -14.4°C.
Is there a free option for lower incomes?
Yes. Income-qualified customers can apply for free upgrades through the Energy Conservation Assistance Program.
